project_capsule.eyebrow: GI tract screening · no tube, no sedation
project_capsule.title: Anhan AI magnetically guided capsule endoscopy
project_capsule.summary: A capsule a touch bigger than a leading fish-oil tablet records the stomach and bowel as it moves naturally, then leaves the body on its own. No sedation, no tube.
project_capsule.feature_1_body: Magnetic positioning and an imaging AI model flag suspicious frames for physician review.
project_capsule.feature_2_body: You swallow the capsule with a sip of water. There is no traditional endoscope and no anesthesia.
project_capsule.feature_3_body: The capsule is a single-use medical device. It exits naturally and is not recovered or reused.
project_capsule.who_body: Adults with upper abdominal discomfort, chronic gastritis follow-up, a family history of gastric cancer, or anyone avoiding conventional endoscopy. Pregnant patients and people with implanted pacemakers should consult their physician first.
preparation_bullets: Eat only clear or semi-liquid food the day before and fast for 8 to 10 hours
Stop iron and bismuth-containing medicines 3 days ahead
People with diabetes should adjust medication with their physician in advance
process_steps: Sign the consent form and put on the data recorder belt
Swallow the capsule with a small sip of water
Magnetic guidance captures images of the stomach and bowel
Physician reads the images with AI support, report in 3 to 5 business days
The capsule exits naturally; no recovery needed
project_capsule.risk_body: Capsule retention is rare but possible. People with known bowel obstruction or severe strictures should not have this test. Avoid strong magnetic fields on the day of the test.

project_cardiac.eyebrow: Coronary screening · no radiation, no contrast
project_cardiac.title: Cardiac MR angiography (MRCA)
project_cardiac.summary: A 3.0T MRI scanner images the coronary arteries without iodinated contrast and without ionizing radiation, suitable for repeat follow-up.
project_cardiac.feature_1_body: Magnetic imaging replaces X-rays, so it can be used for routine follow-up.
project_cardiac.feature_2_body: No iodinated or gadolinium contrast is injected, which suits people with allergies or reduced kidney function.
project_cardiac.feature_3_body: Each scan needs a 14-second breath hold. The full study takes 30 to 45 minutes.
project_cardiac.who_body: Adults with chest tightness, chest pain, or a family history of coronary disease; people allergic to CT contrast who wish to reduce radiation exposure; anyone with an abnormal screening ECG needing further evaluation.
preparation_bullets: Skip caffeine on the day of the test
Practice a 14-second breath hold and follow the technician's rhythm
Pacemakers, implantable defibrillators, and aneurysm clips are contraindications; disclose implants in advance
process_steps: Sign the consent form and remove metal accessories
Practice the breath-hold rhythm and connect the ECG gating leads
Multiple angle scans inside the bore
Physician reads and post-processes the images, report in 2 to 3 business days
Physician reviews the report with you in person or by video
project_cardiac.risk_body: MRI itself produces no ionizing radiation, but implanted metal can be affected by the magnetic field. Disclose all prior surgeries and implants before the scan.
